sections.commentary_text: AUM closed the quarter at ₹1,113 Cr, an increase of ₹23 Cr or 2.1% over the preceding quarter and 5.6% over the same quarter a year earlier. Disbursements were ₹263 Cr against ₹260 Cr in the preceding quarter. Growth was led by Retail Loans and SME Loans, which together contributed the majority of the increase in book size. The Gold Loans portfolio continued to reduce as a share of AUM, consistent with the calibrated run-down the board reviewed in Q2 FY26.

Gross NPA improved to 2.00% from 2.08% in the preceding quarter and 2.36% a year earlier. Net NPA was 1.10% against 1.14%. Provision coverage was 45.5%. Stage 2 assets rose to ₹71.2 Cr from ₹68.4 Cr, with the increase concentrated in the Commercial Vehicle book. Net new flow into Stage 3 was ₹4.9 Cr for the quarter. Collection efficiency across the portfolio was stable.

Revenue for the quarter was ₹382 Cr, 1.0% above the preceding quarter. EBITDA was ₹71 Cr and profit after tax was ₹44 Cr. The EBITDA margin was 18.7%, broadly unchanged. Operating expenses were ₹62.0 Cr. No exceptional items were recognised during the quarter.

The cost of funds rose to 8.30% from 8.24% in the preceding quarter and 8.04% a year earlier, reflecting the repricing of floating-rate bank facilities following the change in the policy rate. Total borrowings stood at ₹897.6 Cr against net worth of ₹253.4 Cr.

AUM stood at ₹1,113 Cr, 2.1% higher than the preceding quarter. Profit after tax was ₹44 Cr. Gross NPA improved to 2.00% from 2.08%, the fourth consecutive quarter of improvement, while Stage 2 assets increased. The cost of funds rose 6 basis points to 8.30%. Two items were placed before the board: the increase in Stage 2 exposure in the Commercial Vehicle book, and a variance between provision coverage computed from the segment ledger and the figure reported by the ECL engine.
